moduleTitle: Lesson 10 - Self-Created SOAP in the API Scan
learningObjectives: Prepare messages from a service specification before an implementation is available.
Distinguish preparation or simulation from testing a real server.
Configure binding-specific headers, method and envelope.
Use formatting without mistaking it for validation.

elements.text: Independent shift-left guidance: prepare an operation payload and expected assertions from an agreed specification before implementation. Live behavior cannot be tested without an available endpoint; a simulator only tests its configured model. Record that distinction explicitly.

API Scan supports creating a message in a project folder and editing its payload and endpoint. Set the method, authentication and headers from the actual binding; manual preparation does not prove the service accepts them.

SOAP 1.2 HTTP uses application/soap+xml, with an optional action parameter. Do not assume the SOAP 1.1 SOAPAction header is universally required for SOAP 1.2. Keep the envelope namespace and binding consistent with the contract.

Pretty Print formats the visible payload; it is not schema validation, a server request or a repair of business errors. Independent guidance: inspect whitespace-sensitive content and signed XML rather than promise all formatting is semantically harmless.

Use the documented API TestCase export for selected messages, then define attributes and assertions. Generate defaults, inspect references and configure input values. Do not infer that every manually prepared message has the same response artifacts or valid selectors as a live scan.

Independent readiness checklist: confirm endpoint access, binding, credentials, payload schema, returned identity and positive/negative assertions. Only execute when an authorized endpoint or documented simulation exists.

Prepare a disposable SOAP operation from a contract and document which checks are static preparation, simulated execution and actual service execution. Academy video/exercise material was inaccessible.

examPitfalls.title: Calling preparation a live test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Claiming server verification before a server or simulation exists.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Label preparation, simulation and real endpoint execution separately.

examPitfalls.title: Treating formatting as validation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Pretty Print proves schema or business correctness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use actual validation and assertions; inspect whitespace-sensitive or signed content.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming one header pattern for all SOAP
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding SOAPAction without checking the SOAP version and binding.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure version-specific media type/action and the service security contract.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When can preparing a SOAP message manually be useful?

options.text: When a specification exists but implementation is not yet available; live execution still requires an endpoint.
Only when internet access is absent.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Preparation can begin early without falsely claiming live service validation.

optionExplanations.B: Offline status is not the only reason.
optionExplanations.C: Manual preparation is a valid workflow.
optionExplanations.D: SOAP can also be prepared from a contract.

options.text: Readable formatting of the visible payload, not schema or service correctness.
It validates the live service and fixes errors.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Inspect correctness separately, including whitespace-sensitive content.

optionExplanations.A: This describes formatting without a universal semantic guarantee.
optionExplanations.B: Pretty Print is not live service validation.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting does not change architectural style.
optionExplanations.D: Business-field removal is not its purpose.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After exporting a manually prepared message, what should the tester do?

options.text: Inspect generated references, configure attributes and assert behavior against an available authorized endpoint or simulation.
Assume execution can never be performed.
Assume every message permanently lacks response artifacts.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect what was generated and what can be executed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manual creation does not eliminate inspection, mapping or endpoint prerequisites.

optionExplanations.A: This addresses preparation and execution readiness.
optionExplanations.B: Exported messages can use Module Attributes.
optionExplanations.C: Execution is possible with the required environment.
optionExplanations.D: A universal missing-response rule is unsupported.

quickRecap.value: Specification-based authoring before implementation, not proof of server behavior.
Set envelope, method, media type/action and security from the contract.
Formatting, not validation; inspect sensitive XML content.
Inspect generated Modules and configure assertions.
Needs an authorized endpoint or documented simulation.
